news.title: Burnham's golden plan: Britain launches a huge bid to bring back the World Cup
news.lede: Britain is set to enter the race to host the 2038 or 2042 World Cup finals, a move that could rewrite the history of football in its birthplace. It is seen as a golden opportunity to bring the biggest tournament in the world back to British soil for the first time since 1966. Andy Burnham is driving this British political ambition, according to Britain's " The Sun ". He sees hosting the World Cup not merely as a sporting event, but as an integrated national project capable of triggering an unprecedented boom in tourism, investment and infrastructure across the whole country.Six full decades have passed since that immortal afternoon at the old Wembley Stadium.

news.title: Argentina star handed 10-match ban for attacking Spain player after World Cup final
news.lede: Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes attacked Spain midfielder Gavi after Argentina’s defeat (EPA) Leandro Paredes has been handed a ten-match ban as several Argentina players were punished for their role in the disgraceful brawl following the World Cup 2026 final against Spain. The Argentina midfielder was seen grabbing Spain’s Eric Garcia by the throat before throwing Barcelona’s Gavi to the ground. In separate incidents, Argentina defender Nahuel Molina appeared to strike Spain captain Rodri as he ran onto the pitch to celebrate at full-time, while assistant coach Ayala was captured punching Dani Olmo in the face after a brief verbal spat. Molina has been dealt a seven-match ban, while Ayala has been suspended for three matches.

news.title: Argentina star slapped with 10-MATCH ban as FIFA announce World Cup punishments
news.lede: FIFA has banned Argentina duo Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina for their parts in the brawl that occurred following the World Cup final . Paredes has been hit with a mammoth 10-match ban whilst Nahuel Molina has been handed a ban of seven matches. One-match bans have been handed down to Thiago Almada and Pablo Martín Páez Gavira. Paredes and Molina both copped particular criticism for their reactions after Argentina were beaten 1-0 by Spain in the final in New York.

news.title: Leandro Paredes hit with giant FIFA ban as three Argentina players punished over World Cup shame
news.lede: Paredes has also been fined $90,000 for his role in the incident, which saw him throw punches and attack Spain players. He is not the only Argentinian player to be punished either, with FIFA handing out suspensions to Thiago Almada and Nahuel Molina. Almada has been banned for one game and fined $30,000, with Molina fined $90,000 and banned for seven matches for their roles in the clash with their rivals at the World Cup in July. Argentina coach Roberto Ayala was also hit with a three-match suspension and a fine of $30,000, while Spain star Gavi has been handed a one-match ban for his role in the incident too.

news.title: World Cup 2026: Argentina's Paredes banned for 10 games over World Cup final clashes
news.lede: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes has been given a 10-match ban for the role he played in on-field clashes after his side were beaten 1-0 by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. Fifa's disciplinary committee has also handed his team-mate Nahuel Molina a seven-match suspension. Argentina have also been ordered to play their next two home matches behind closed doors, though one match of that sanction is suspended. When the World Cup finishes, the football continues on BBC Sport.

news.title: Three Argentina players banned over brawl after World Cup final defeat
news.lede: Three Argentina players have been banned for their part in a brawl at the end of last month’s World Cup final against Spain, but the South American nation have only been fined for displaying a Falkland Islands banner after the semi-final win over England. Midfielder Leandro Paredes has been hit hardest and given a 10-match ban and a 90,000 US Dollars (£66,000) fine by FIFA’s disciplinary committee, while defender Nahuel Molina was given a seven-match suspension and fined the same amount. Thiago Almada was given a one-match ban and a 30,000 USD (£22,000) fine, while Argentina coach Roberto Ayala was banned for three matches and fined the same amount. Spain’s Gavi has also been given a one-match ban and a 30,000 USD fine.
